name: MCP3002 2-channel 10-bit ADC (SPI)
description: Microchip 10-bit successive-approximation analog-to-digital converter with 2 single-ended inputs (or 1 pseudo-differential pair) and an SPI interface, up to 200 ksps at 5 V (75 ksps at 2.7 V). VDD is also the reference: Code = 1024 x VIN / VDD. Runs on 2.7-5.5 V. Sold as: MCP3002-I/P bare chip in a DIP-8 package (pin 1 CS/SHDN, 2 CH0, 3 CH1, 4 VSS, 5 DIN, 6 DOUT, 7 CLK, 8 VDD/VREF), plugged straight into a breadboard.
eli5: Gives your board two analog inputs: it measures two voltages and sends the numbers over SPI.

pins.name: CS/SHDN
pins.description: Chip select / shutdown, active low (pin 1). Must go high between conversions

pins.name: CH0
pins.description: Analog input 0 (pin 2), 0 V to VDD; never above VDD + 0.6 V

pins.name: CH1
pins.description: Analog input 1 (pin 3), 0 V to VDD; never above VDD + 0.6 V

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: Serial data in: start bit, SGL/DIFF, ODD/SIGN and MSBF bits (pin 5)

pins.name: DOUT
pins.description: Serial data out: null bit then the 10-bit result (pin 6)

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: Serial clock, 10 kHz to 1.2 MHz at 2.7 V, 3.2 MHz at 5 V (pin 7)

pins.name: VDD/VREF
pins.description: Supply AND reference, 2.7-5.5 V (pin 8): sets full scale. Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico for 0-3.3 V inputs and 3.3 V logic

buildNotes: Send 2 bytes in SPI mode 0: 0x68 for CH0 or 0x78 for CH1 (start, single-ended, MSB first), then 0x00. The result is (reply[0] & 0x03) << 8 | reply[1]; the upper bits of reply[0] are undefined (high-Z, then the null bit).
Pull CS/SHDN high after every conversion: each conversion starts with a new CS falling edge.
There is no separate VREF pin: VDD is the reference, so volts = code x VDD / 1024. A noisy supply means noisy readings.
Power it from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico; at 5 V DOUT would drive 5 V into a 3.3 V GPIO.
Keep SPI clock between 10 kHz and 1.2 MHz at 2.7-3.3 V (3.2 MHz max at 5 V); too slow and the sample capacitor droops.
Put a 1 uF ceramic capacitor from VDD/VREF to VSS close to the chip.
Analog sources above about 1 kohm need a slower clock (datasheet Figure 4-2) or a buffer.

driver.code:
# MCP3002 2-channel 10-bit SPI ADC (Microchip MCP3002, DS21294E), MicroPython driver.
# Uses the datasheet's 2-byte, 8-bit-aligned transfer (Section 6.1, Figure 6-1, SPI mode 0,0):
#   sent:     0 START SGL/DIFF ODD/SIGN MSBF x x x | x x x x x x x x
#   received: ? ? ? ? ? NULL B9 B8                 | B7 B6 B5 B4 B3 B2 B1 B0
# The leading zero before the start bit puts the 10-bit result in the low bits.
# VDD is also the reference: Code = 1024 * VIN / VDD (Section 4.2).
from machine import Pin


class MCP3002:
    def __init__(self, spi, cs, vdd=3.3):
        """spi: machine.SPI in mode 0 (polarity=0, phase=0), 10 kHz to 1.2 MHz at 2.7 V
        (3.2 MHz max at 5 V). cs: GPIO number of CS/SHDN. vdd: voltage on the VDD/VREF pin."""
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.vdd = vdd
        self._tx = bytearray(2)
        self._rx = bytearray(2)

    def read_raw(self, channel, single_ended=True):
        """Convert one channel and return the 10-bit code (0-1023).
        single_ended=False selects pseudo-differential mode (Table 5-1):
        channel 0 = CH0 is IN+ / CH1 is IN-, channel 1 = CH1 is IN+ / CH0 is IN-."""
        if channel not in (0, 1):
            raise ValueError('MCP3002 channel must be 0 or 1')
        # 0b0 1 SGL ODD MSBF 000: start bit, mode, channel, MSB-first only
        self._tx[0] = 0x40 | (0x20 if single_ended else 0x00) | (channel << 4) | 0x08
        self._tx[1] = 0x00
        self.cs.value(0)
        self.spi.write_readinto(self._tx, self._rx)
        self.cs.value(1)  # CS must go high between conversions (tCSH >= 310 ns)
        return ((self._rx[0] & 0x03) << 8) | self._rx[1]

    def raw_to_volts(self, raw):
        return raw * self.vdd / 1024

    def read_volts(self, channel, single_ended=True):
        return self.raw_to_volts(self.read_raw(channel, single_ended))

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from mcp3002 import MCP3002

spi = SPI(1, baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CLK}), mosi=Pin({DIN}), miso=Pin({DOUT}))
adc = MCP3002(spi, {CS_SHDN}, vdd=3.3)  # VDD/VREF on 3.3 V
while True:
    r0 = adc.read_raw(0)
    r1 = adc.read_raw(1)
    print('CH0=%d %.3fV CH1=%d %.3fV' % (r0, adc.raw_to_volts(r0), r1, adc.raw_to_volts(r1)))
    time.sleep(1)
